task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently at home in the United States.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output:
User: Hello, yes... I'm having trouble with my phone. My mobile data — the internet on my phone when I'm not on Wi-Fi — it either stops working completely or it's just so terribly slow. I'd really like to get it working properly.

I should mention, I don't have any Wi-Fi at home, so I'm relying on the mobile data entirely.

turns.thought:
Thank you, Mr. Smith — I've found your account (customer ID **C1001**).

I've checked your line **555-123-2002** (line L1002), and here's what I can see on the account side:

- **Line status:** Active
- **Data used this cycle:** 8.7 GB out of your 15 GB Premium Plan allowance (cycle ends 2025-02-28) — so you haven't hit your data cap
- **Roaming:** already enabled
- **Bills:** no overdue bills on the account

So everything on our end looks healthy — which means the problem is most likely on your phone itself or with the network signal where you are.

To help me pin it down, could you tell me what you see at the **very top of your screen** (the status bar)? Specifically:

1. Do you see signal bars at all, or does it say "No Signal"?
2. Do you see an **airplane icon** ✈️ anywhere?
3. Do you see a **keyhole/VPN icon** 🔒 or a **down-arrow "data saver" icon** 🔽?
4. When the internet "stops completely", does it come back on its own after a while, or only after you restart the phone?

Any of those details will help me narrow it down quickly. And if you'd rather not fiddle with the settings yourself, just say the word and I'll connect you with a technical specialist who can run remote diagnostics on your device.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me look at the top of my screen for you. One moment...

turns.thought:
No need to worry at all — you haven't broken anything! That's actually great news, and here's why: **Airplane Mode is almost certainly the whole problem.**

When Airplane Mode is on, your phone deliberately switches off all of its wireless connections — cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth. That's why you're seeing no signal bars at all. It's very easy to switch on by accident, often just by brushing the wrong icon when you pull down the notification shade at the top of the screen.

**Here's how to turn it off:**

1. From the very top of your screen, **swipe downward** (usually with one finger, from the top edge) — this opens your Quick Settings panel.
2. Look for the **airplane icon** in that grid of round buttons. It's probably lit up or highlighted while it's active.
3. **Tap that airplane icon once.** It should go dim/grey, and the ✈️ symbol at the top of your screen should disappear.
4. Wait about 10–20 seconds. Your signal bars should reappear, and your mobile data should start working again.

Could you give that a try now and let me know what you see at the top of your screen afterwards? I'd especially like to know:

- Do the **signal bars** come back?
- Do you see a network type like **5G**, **4G**, or **LTE** next to them?

Once you tell me that, I'll know whether we've solved it or whether there's something else we should look at.
turns.execution_output: User: All right, let me try to find that airplane button... I'm pulling down from the top of the screen now.

turns.thought:
Excellent — that's real progress! Airplane Mode is off, so we've cleared the biggest hurdle. And you've actually spotted the two remaining causes yourself. Here's what they mean:

- **"Data Disabled"** — this is why your internet *stops completely*. Your mobile data switch is turned off, so the phone isn't allowed to use the cellular network for internet at all.
- **"2G"** — 2G is a very old, very slow type of network. It's fine for basic calls and texts, but it's far too slow for internet browsing or apps. That's exactly why things crawl when they do connect.
- **"Poor" (one bar)** — that's just the signal strength where you are right now, and it often improves once we get off 2G.

Nothing is broken. Let's fix them one at a time.

---

### Step 1: Turn Mobile Data back ON

1. Open your phone's **Settings** app (the gear icon).
2. Tap **Network & internet** — on some phones this is called **Connections**.
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or *SIMs* / *Mobile data*).
4. Find the switch labelled **Mobile data** and tap it so it turns **ON** (it'll usually slide right or light up).

If it's easier, there's often a quicker way: **swipe down from the top of your screen twice** to open your Quick Settings again, and look for a tile labelled **Mobile data** — tap it to switch it on.

---

Could you try that and tell me what the top of your screen shows afterwards? Specifically, does it now say **"Data Enabled"**?

Once that's sorted, I'll walk you through switching off the slow 2G connection — that should make a big difference to your speed.
turns.execution_output: User: All right, I'll try to turn the mobile data on. Let me see if I can find that switch...

turns.thought:
You're asking exactly the right questions — please don't apologise! And you've spotted two more real issues, yes.

**Yes, Data Saver is another culprit.** It's a feature designed to reduce how much data your phone uses. It does that by stopping apps from refreshing in the background and by restricting data in ways that can make browsing and apps feel sluggish or seem to "hang." It's not harmful, but it definitely makes things feel slower. Let's switch it off.

### Step 1: Turn Data Saver OFF

1. Open **Settings** (the gear icon).
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or **Connections**).
3. Tap **Data Saver** — on some phones it's under **Mobile network** first.
4. Tap the switch so Data Saver turns **OFF**.

If you're asked to confirm, choose **Turn off** / **OK**.

---

### Step 2: Move off the slow 2G network

This one is likely the biggest cause of your slow speeds. 2G is an old network type that simply isn't built for modern internet — even at full signal it would feel painfully slow. Your line and plan fully support faster networks, so let's tell your phone to prefer them:

1. In **Settings**, tap **Network & internet** (or **Connections**).
2. Tap **Mobile network** (or **SIMs**).
3. Look for **Preferred network mode** or **Network mode** — it probably shows "2G" or "2G/3G" right now.
4. Tap it and choose the option that mentions **5G and 4G** — something like **"5G/4G/3G/2G auto"** or **"5G preferred"** or **"4G/5G auto connect."** (If you see several options, pick the *highest* one, e.g. anything starting with 5G.)

Your phone may drop the signal for a few seconds while it switches, then reconnect.

---

### Step 3: Restart your phone

Once you've done both of the above, please **restart (power off and on)** your phone. This lets all the changes take effect properly, and it often helps the phone latch onto the best available signal — which may well improve that "Poor / one bar" reading too.

---

Could you work through those three steps and then tell me what the top of your screen shows? I'm looking for:

- **"Data Saver"** gone
- A network type of **4G / 5G / LTE** instead of 2G
- Ideally more than one **signal bar**

If the signal is still "Poor" after all that, we can try a couple more things — and if it turns out your home is simply in a weak coverage spot, there are options for that too.
turns.execution_output: User: Oh my, that's three things at once... I'm afraid I can only manage one at a time, I get a bit muddled otherwise. Let me do the first one — turning off that Data Saver.

turns.thought:
Those are completely reasonable worries, and I'm glad you asked before jumping in. Let me put your mind at rest on both counts:

**Your phone calls will be fine.** Changing the network mode doesn't turn anything off — it just tells your phone, "When you have a choice, pick the faster network." Your phone keeps 3G and 2G available in the background as a backup, so if you're ever somewhere without 4G or 5G, it will still connect for calls and texts. Nothing gets switched off that you rely on.

**Your photos are completely safe.** Photos live in your phone's storage — the same place they are right now. Changing a network setting has absolutely nothing to do with your pictures, and nothing will be deleted or moved. Your photos of your grandchildren are not at risk.

Honestly, of everything we've done today, this is one of the safest changes. And you can always switch it back exactly the same way if you don't like it.

---

### When you're ready — here's how to change it

1. Open **Settings** (the gear icon).
2. Tap **Network & internet** — on some phones this is called **Connections**.
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or **SIMs**).
4. Find **Preferred network mode** or **Network mode** — it'll likely show "2G" right now.
5. Tap it, and choose the option that includes **5G** — something like **"5G/4G/3G/2G auto"** or **"5G preferred."** If you don't see a 5G option, pick **"4G/3G/2G auto"** or **"LTE."**

Your signal may disappear for 5–10 seconds and then come back — that's completely normal, it's just your phone reconnecting to a better network.

**Then please restart your phone** (hold the power button, choose Restart / Power off, then switch it back on). This helps the new setting take effect properly, and it often helps your phone find a stronger signal too.

---

Take your time, there's no rush at all. When you've done it, tell me what the top of your screen says — I'm hoping to see **4G, 5G or LTE** there instead of 2G, and hopefully more than one bar.

And if you'd rather not change it yourself, that's genuinely fine — I can arrange for a technical specialist to walk you through it over the phone, or look at it remotely. Just say so and I'll set that up for you.
turns.execution_output: User: Well, you've reassured me about my photos, thank you. Let me try it then. I'm going into the settings... looking for the network mode...

turns.thought:
That's wonderful news — yes, that's exactly what we were hoping for! **Four bars, "Excellent," and 5G** means your phone has latched onto the fastest network available to you. Going from "Poor / 2G / Data Disabled" to "Excellent / 5G / Data Enabled" should feel like a completely different phone when you browse.

**On the restart — no, it won't lose anything.** A restart simply turns your phone off and back on again. Everything stays exactly where it is: your photos, your contacts, your messages, your apps. It's the same phone with the same contents, just with a fresh start. Think of it like switching a lamp off and on again — the lamp and everything in the room is unchanged.

**Do you need to right now?** Honestly, since it's already showing 5G and Excellent, you could happily skip it and just start using your data. But I'd still gently recommend it when it's convenient, for two reasons:

1. It lets all the settings changes we made "settle in" properly, so they stick.
2. It clears out any temporary glitches that might have built up from the earlier Airplane Mode and Data Saver changes.

If it's easier, you can leave it until tonight or whenever you'd next switch your phone off anyway — there's no urgency.

---

**Could you try something for me?** Since your data is now on, try opening a webpage or an app that needs the internet — maybe a news site or your email. Let me know:

- Does it load?
- Does it feel quicker than before?

If it's working well, then we're all done. If it's still sluggish despite the 5G and four bars, tell me and we'll look at the next couple of things together — and if we can't get it sorted, I'll arrange for a technical specialist to take a proper look for you.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me try that speed check thing... I'll see what it says.

turns.thought:
You are so welcome — what lovely news! 275 Mbps and pages loading straight away is a brilliant result, and all credit to you for working through each of those steps so carefully. You didn't break anything at all.

And yes, leaving the restart until tonight when you'd switch your phone off anyway is perfectly fine — it'll do just as much good then.

For your reference, here's a quick summary of what we found and fixed on your line **555-123-2002**:

1. **Airplane Mode was ON** — this was why you had no signal at all. Turned off.
2. **Mobile Data was OFF** — this was why the internet stopped completely. Turned on.
3. **Data Saver was ON** — this was slowing things down. Turned off.
4. **Network mode was set to 2G** — an old, very slow network type. Changed to 5G.

A couple of reassuring notes:
- **No change to your plan or bill.** No charges were made, and nothing on your account was altered.
- **Your data allowance is in good shape** — 8.7 GB used of your 15 GB allowance, and your cycle refreshes on 28 February, so you have plenty left.

If the problem ever comes back, checking for that ✈️ airplane symbol first is usually the quickest way to spot the cause.

Enjoy your faster internet, and those photos of your grandchildren should now upload and share nicely too. Do get in touch any time if anything else comes up — you take care!
